scope_note: QA Harmonic Aliquot Structure cert [322]. Primary source: Iverson, B. (1995) Quantum Arithmetic Book 3 (QA-3), ITAM Portland, ISBN 1-883401-08-9, Chapter 4: 'HARMONICS'. Theory of Harmony (p.52): 'Harmonics, or harmony occurs between two dissimilar cycles of energy when both can be divided into similar aliquot parts having the same magnitude but different multitudes.' Formal QA translation: two waves W1=A*p1 and W2=A*p2 are harmonic iff A=gcd(W1,W2), p1=W1/A and p2=W2/A are distinct primes, and gcd(A,p1*p2)=1. Scope boundary: this cert includes both a mod-9 Cosmos test model and source-native completed-wave witnesses, but it does not certify the entire QA-3 energy-transport doctrine. In the test model, d-value d=b+e is treated as the semi-major diameter (DO=d*d from cert [320]); the 15 distinct Cosmos d-values {3,...,17} are the enumerated harmonic domain. Structural results certified: (C1) 20 harmonic dyads among Cosmos d-values; all aliquot parts 7-smooth. (C2) Direction law: for every dyad with d1<d2, p2>p1. (C3) Aliquot spectrum is exactly {1,2,3,5}. (C4) 5040=2^4*3^2*5*7 has omega=4 distinct prime factors; all Cosmos d-values <= 17 < 5040. (C5) Exactly 3 Cosmos d-values are primes > 7: {11,13,17}; each forms 5 harmonic dyads. (C6) Completed-wave witnesses validate W=A*p where A is the product of all non-unique prime factors, p is a unique prime not inside A, A>p, and factor counts match declared 5/7-wave structure. (C7) Shared-aliquot harmony validates gcd(W1,W2)=A for waves with the same aliquot core and distinct unique primes. Negative probes reject too-small aliquot, unique-prime-inside-aliquot, and mismatched aliquot cores. Builds on cert [320] (Quantize Algorithm, DO=d*d) and cert [321] (Quantize-to-ONE, ratio b/a). Complements cert [318] (Synchronous Harmonics Ceiling, 5040 extremal). DOI: primary text, no external DOI.
